title: Purge legacy rollout paths, flags, and old API endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Remove deprecated rollout code paths, legacy feature flags, and old /v1/rollout API endpoints that were kept for backward compatibility with pre-2023 clients. This ticket coordinates the runtime, router, and console changes required to safely retire these artifacts and clean up config schema versions.

Goals:
- Eliminate dead code and simplify runtime config parsing (reduce maintenance overhead).
- Remove legacy endpoints (/v1/rollout/*) and migrate remaining callers to /v2/rollouts.
- Delete legacy feature flags: use_legacy_rollout, enable_kv_v1, routing_hack_fallback.
- Consolidate config schema: bump rollout_config from v1beta -> v2 and validate at startup.
- Ensure zero customer-facing disruptions via canary + metric-backed verification.

Scope (non-exhaustive):
- runtime: remove branching logic for use_legacy_rollout and enable_kv_v1; update config loader to error on v1 schema when runtime.runtime.strict_schema is enabled.
- router: deprecate /v1/rollout endpoints and add 410 responses for calls with X-Deprecation: warn header after canary window.
- console: delete UI toggle for legacy rollouts and migration notice in release notes.
- SDKs: add explicit migration warnings in SDK logs (separate PR in sdk repo).

Acceptance criteria:
- All code paths guarded by the three legacy flags are removed from the runtime branch.
- No internal service calls to /v1/rollout exist (scanned via grep and service map).
- CI passes with config v2 schema validation enabled.
- Canary release on dedicated pool for 48h with no increase in latency/errors beyond baseline.
- Documentation and runbook updated with rollback steps.

Rollback plan:
- If canary metrics fail, automatically re-enable compatibility mode via runtime feature flip on dedicated pool (requires ENG-7899 rollback helper).
- Hotfix: reintroduce compatibility shim (short-lived) with toggles for safe unrolling.

Notes and rationale:
- These legacy flags were originally introduced as short-term mitigations for the 2022 rollout of the new KV cache. Several months of telemetry showed near-zero usage of legacy clients; the flags have since become maintenance burden and a source of subtle bugs (see incident IN-2024-11).
- Replacing the /v1/rollout surface reduces attack surface and simplifies routing rules that currently require dual-path validation.

Testing plan:
1) Unit tests: add negative tests to ensure v1 schema is rejected when strict_schema is true.
2) Integration tests: spin up router+runtime private stack and verify /v2/rollouts succeeds while /v1/rollout returns 410 when deprecation is live.
3) Canary: deploy to 5% traffic on dedicated pool, monitor latency, error-rate, and rollout-failure metrics for 48h.

Metrics to watch:
- rollout_api_5xx_rate
- rollout_api_duration_p95
- backlog_kv_cache_miss_rate
- rollout_migration_failures

Related artifacts and links:

- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Rt_example_doc/view (internal)
- Runtime PR (cleanup): https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/1342
- Router PR (deprecate endpoints): https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/418
